catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Structural, domain, and behavioral architecture analysis of cas_runner and continuous architecture governance system excluding agentic prompt/LLM-interaction patterns.
analysis_limits: Dynamic runtime evaluation restricted to static analysis of key Python modules and directory layout.
Omitted all agentic AI prompting and LLM loop orchestration mechanics per scope definition.

system_map.overview: The Continuous Architecture System (CAS) CLI Runner (`cas_runner`) is structured as a modular layered architecture. It decouples interface concerns (CLI), service-layer workflows, domain modeling (Pydantic-based governance records and telemetry spans), and infrastructure adapters (file-based knowledge management, telemetry normalization adapters, and external client wrappers).

layers.name: presentation
layers.purpose: Command-line interface and terminal interaction rendering using Rich.

layers.name: application
layers.purpose: Workflow execution orchestration, bootstrapping workspaces, and service-level coordination.

layers.name: domain
layers.purpose: Core governance entities, state machine transition registries, compliance calculation, and health aggregation models.

layers.name: infrastructure
layers.purpose: External provider clients, trace normalization adapters, and hierarchical filesystem knowledge repositories.

components.name: GovernanceActionEngine
components.responsibility: Executes state transitions and policy rules on governance entities via registered transitions.

components.name: AgentTelemetryAdapterRegistry
components.responsibility: Normalizes multi-provider telemetry events into unified AgentTelemetrySpan models.

components.name: WorkspaceBootstrapper
components.responsibility: Scaffolds local workspace environments, symlinks knowledge templates, and manages settings merging.

orchestration.execution_style: Synchronous CLI task execution via FlowRunner and GovernanceActionService invoking domain engines.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity and Metric Modeling
patterns.summary: Encapsulates governance artifacts, compliance findings, and traceable metrics into strongly-typed Pydantic domain models with built-in runtime validation.
patterns.intent: Ensure schema integrity, strong typing, and deterministic serialization across governance checks and health aggregation.
patterns.context: The system processes governance inventories, architectural decisions, and compliance findings across local file structures and CI pipelines.
forces: Data ingested from heterogeneous Markdown and YAML files can be malformed or incomplete.
Downstream metrics calculations need guaranteed typed attributes without pervasive defensive checks.
patterns.solution: Define data transfer objects and domain aggregates (such as ResolutionResult, GovernanceInventory, ComplianceFinding, TraceableMetric) as Pydantic models ensuring parse-time invariant validation.
implementation_signals: Subclasses of pydantic.BaseModel defining domain schemas
Field-level validation and explicit type annotations
Clean decoupling between business models and presentation layers

evidence.note: Complete domain aggregate and value object definitions modeling architecture governance metrics and actions.

benefits: Zero-cost schema validation at domain boundaries.
Self-documenting data models easily serialized to JSON/YAML for reports.
costs: Runtime validation overhead on large volume ingestions.
Tight coupling of domain data structures to Pydantic v2.
failure_modes: Validation errors thrown abruptly during processing of legacy or non-conforming knowledge files.

patterns.reuse_notes: Directly reusable in any architecture linter or metrics collector requiring validated schema contracts.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Decouples state transition declarations from execution logic using a centralized TransitionRegistry consumed by an action execution engine.
patterns.intent: Constrain governance artifact lifecycles (e.g., draft, review, approved, retired) to verified, deterministic state changes.
patterns.context: Governance actions must mutate artifact status and trigger validation without hardcoding transition paths inside command handlers.
forces: Ad-hoc mutations lead to invalid governance states (e.g. promoting unreviewed heuristics to patterns).
Adding new states or action triggers should not require modifying the execution dispatcher.
patterns.solution: Register permissible source-to-target transitions and guards inside a TransitionRegistry, which the GovernanceActionEngine queries before executing state mutations.
implementation_signals: Explicit registry class or dictionary of valid source/target pairs and handler hooks
Separation of transition validation from transition execution

evidence.note: Registry defining allowed governance transitions executed by the action engine.

benefits: Centralized validation of valid domain state permutations.
Extensible registration of custom transition validation rules without engine changes.
costs: Requires explicit initialization and registration wiring before command execution.
failure_modes: Attempting an unmapped transition raises runtime exceptions if not gracefully caught.

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable across document approval lifecycles, ADR management, and architectural risk mitigation workflows.

patterns.name: Adapter-Based Telemetry Normalization
patterns.summary: Normalizes diverse upstream agent and runtime telemetry outputs into standard AgentTelemetrySpan structures using specialized adapter implementations.
patterns.intent: Isolate the dashboard and health calculation engine from vendor-specific telemetry trace formats and timestamps.
patterns.context: Telemetry data originates from diverse external execution agents (Claude Code, Antigravity, generic coding agents) with differing payload formats and timestamp standards.
forces: Dashboard metrics require consistent ISO epoch dates and standardized duration and cost fields.
External trace formats change independently of the internal health monitoring system.
patterns.solution: Define concrete adapter classes (e.g., ClaudeCodeTelemetryAdapter, AntigravityTelemetryAdapter) conforming to a common protocol that ingest raw event streams and produce unified AgentTelemetrySpan objects.
implementation_signals: Multiple adapter classes sharing common normalization methods
Dedicated parsing functions for ISO timestamps and cost estimations

evidence.note: Adapters translating specific agent traces into unified AgentTelemetrySpan models.

benefits: Shields internal reporting models from changes in external tooling formats.
Encapsulates provider cost heuristics and ISO timestamp normalization.
costs: Each newly supported agent provider requires a distinct adapter and unit test coverage.
failure_modes: Unexpected schema variations in vendor logs can lead to silent dropouts or default fallback values.

patterns.reuse_notes: Ideal for observability collectors aggregating events from heterogeneous external tools or CLI assistants.

patterns.name: Service Facade Action Orchestrator
patterns.summary: Exposes a consolidated application service interface coordinating compliance engines, action engines, and persistence layers for presentation callers.
patterns.intent: Prevent CLI commands from directly orchestrating domain rules, engines, and multiple repositories.
patterns.context: The CLI needs to trigger compliance validations, evaluate system health, and persist resolutions without coupling CLI handlers to internal domain logic.
forces: Direct CLI-to-domain coupling makes headless CI automation or alternative runner interfaces difficult to maintain.
Multiple domain engines must be invoked in a coherent transaction-like sequence.
patterns.solution: Implement GovernanceActionService as an application facade that encapsulates transaction ordering, engine delegation, and result gathering.
implementation_signals: Methods taking simple parameters or DTOs and coordinating domain engines

evidence.note: Application service encapsulating governance operations and delegating to domain engines.

benefits: Clear boundary between presentation (CLI/CI) and domain logic.
Simplifies end-to-end testing of business workflows without CLI invocation.
costs: Potential for the service to become an anemic pass-through if business logic leaks into either CLI or engines.
failure_modes: Monolithic service bloat if too many distinct operational domains are placed in one class.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard pattern for CLI tools wrapping complex multi-step domain workflows.

patterns.name: Idempotent Symlink and Scaffolding Bootstrap
patterns.summary: Establishes workspace conventions by creating symlinks, falling back to copies, and merging template configuration blocks non-destructively.
patterns.intent: Initialize target development environments safely and repeatedly without destroying preexisting local configurations.
patterns.context: When onboarding a new repository or workspace, CAS governance files, Claude settings, and directory templates must be linked or copied reliably.
forces: OS-level permission differences or cross-filesystem links may cause symlink creation to fail.
Existing configuration files must be merged rather than blindly overwritten.
patterns.solution: Implement helper functions that verify link capability, fallback to atomic copy operations, and deep-merge configuration blocks with idempotent checkmarks.
implementation_signals: Try-except blocks attempting symlink with copy fallback
Config merge functions that preserve existing dictionary keys
Checklist generation for user onboarding verification

evidence.note: Safely manages filesystem initialization with symlink/copy fallbacks and non-destructive JSON/YAML configuration merging.

benefits: Robust across varied operating environments (macOS, Linux CI, restricted containers).
Idempotent execution allows developers to rerun bootstrap commands without risk of data loss.
costs: Symlink vs copy differences can cause drift if local edits are made to detached file copies.
failure_modes: Divergence between symlinked centralized templates and copied local files in multi-developer setups.

patterns.reuse_notes: Directly reusable in developer tooling, monorepo linters, and repository scaffolding systems.

patterns.name: Pluggable Client Strategy
patterns.summary: Provides mock and live client implementations conforming to a common invocation interface to facilitate fast deterministic testing and offline execution.
patterns.intent: Decouple external network and gateway dependencies from flow execution and automated tests.
patterns.context: Flow runners need to interact with external inference or validation services, but CI and local test suites cannot depend on live credentials or billable endpoints.
forces: External services are slow, nondeterministic, and require network access.
End-to-end integration tests must run reliably in isolated environments.
patterns.solution: Implement a shared interface satisfied by both production clients (LiteLLMClient) and deterministic test stubs (MockLLMClient).
implementation_signals: Parallel client classes providing equivalent call/completion signatures
Configurable factory or dependency injection supplying the active client to FlowRunner

evidence.note: Deterministic test implementation satisfying the client interface.

benefits: Instant offline unit and functional test execution.
Isolation of third-party SDK dependencies behind a controlled interface.
costs: Mock client behavior can drift from production provider response nuances over time.
failure_modes: Failing to replicate provider error structures in the mock client can mask unhandled production exceptions.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard pattern for external service integration in testable Python systems.

patterns.name: Hierarchical Knowledge Repository Structure
patterns.summary: Organizes architecture documentation and governance state into a strictly segregated filesystem hierarchy separating global rules, project instances, runtime traces, and templates.
patterns.intent: Enable scalable Documentation-as-Code where governance rules, decisions, and runtime metrics are version-controlled alongside code.
patterns.context: Organizations need to maintain global architectural rules while allowing individual projects to retain localized decisions, runtime traces, and compliance records.
forces: Monolithic documentation files become unmanageable and cause merge conflicts.
Runtime telemetry must not pollute global policy standards.
patterns.solution: Partition storage into distinct folders: `global/` (rules, decisions, maps), `governance/` (steering, reviews), `projects/` (project-specific manifests), `runtime/` (traces, evaluations), and `templates/` (canonical markdown templates).
implementation_signals: Dedicated directory trees with clear scoping in cas-knowledge/
Templates directory providing blueprints for all artifact types
Runtime directory reserved for transient evaluation outputs and traces

evidence.note: Directory hierarchy segregating global governance, project instances, runtime traces, and structural templates.

benefits: Clear separation of concerns between normative governance and descriptive runtime data.
Git-native diffing, auditing, and review workflows for all architectural assets.
costs: Deep directory hierarchies require robust path resolution and link maintenance tooling.
failure_modes: Broken internal links when artifacts are moved or renamed without refactoring tools.

patterns.reuse_notes: Highly reusable structural blueprint for architecture-as-code and enterprise knowledge repositories.

anti_patterns.name: Direct Filesystem Drift via Copied Templates
symptoms: Fallback from symlink to copy silently detaches local workspace files from upstream governance updates.
Manual edits to local copies are never synced back to cas-knowledge/templates.
impact: Teams operate against outdated governance rules and template structures without realizing their local version drifted.
suggested_remediation: Implement a checksum or version hash check in the bootstrap verification step to detect drift in copied configuration templates.

anti_patterns.name: Monolithic Service Delegation (God Service)
symptoms: GovernanceActionService accumulating responsibilities across compliance, action dispatching, health modeling, and file persistence.
impact: High coupling in application layer, making unit testing require complex multi-component mocks.
suggested_remediation: Split application services along specific bounded contexts (e.g., ComplianceEvaluationService, HealthAggregationService).

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Telemetry and Cost Observability
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Standardizing trace timestamps, span normalization, and cost estimation across heterogeneous agent executions using OpenTelemetry-compatible structures.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Workspace Configuration Safety
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Ensuring non-destructive file operations and idempotent configuration updates during workspace initialization and CI pipeline runs.

open_questions.question: How are cross-references within `cas-knowledge/global` and `cas-knowledge/projects` validated when files are renamed or deprecated during CI validation?
Does `cas-knowledge/runtime/traces/` have an automated retention/eviction policy, or does it accumulate indefinitely in the repository git history?
